content.Atrial disease evaluation: Atrial size and function can be evaluated by multimodality imaging including two- and three-dimensional echocardiography, myocardial deformation, computed tomography (CT) and CMR. Cardiac biomarkers, including high-sensitivity cardiac troponins and NPs, may assess pathophysiological aspects of atrial disease. Increased levels of NPs in AF may indicate underlying atrial disease. A comprehensive characterization combining clinical, imaging, biochemical and molecular features is currently lacking.
content.Management: Atrial disease is an emerging therapeutic target for prevention of AF, systemic thromboembolism, and possibly HFpEF. Atrial disease results from shared risk factors and comorbidities predisposing to AF and HF: diabetes mellitus, hypertension, obesity, smoking and physical inactivity. Effective management of HF and AF and treatment of mitral regurgitation may help counteract atrial disease progression.
content.Myocarditis - epidemiology and diagnosis: Incidence of acute myocarditis estimated ~1.5 million cases/year globally. Contribution of myocarditis as a cause of HF varies by age and region (~0.5% to 4%). Chronic, EMB-proven inflammation can be found in 9% to 30% of adult patients with DCM.
